correctness.rationale: The proof was reconstructed from the assigned RESULT.md. A final one-block vertex is universal, so \(\gamma_P=1\). For \(v\in B_i\), all one-blocks and zero-blocks through \(A_i\) are initially observed. Any later zero-block of size at least two contains two unobserved false twins, which can never be the first forced vertex; if all later zero-blocks are singletons, successive vertices of \(B_{i+1},B_{i+2},\ldots\) force them in order. For \(v\in A_i\), \(i\ge2\), every observed later one-vertex sees at least one unobserved vertex in \(A_{i-1}\) and one in \(B_{i-1}\), so no force starts. For \(v\in A_1\), the same false-twin obstruction is exact and the singleton-block forcing chain proves sufficiency. I independently replayed the defining closure test for every connected creation sequence of orders \(2\) through \(12\): 2,047 graphs and 22,528 singleton placements, with zero criterion mismatches. The finite replay is corroborative only; the block proof establishes the infinite statement.
correctness.risk: The characterization uses the canonical threshold-block convention and ordinary power domination; it does not classify larger power-dominating sets or propagation times.

final_claim: For a finite connected threshold graph with canonical creation blocks \(0^{a_1}1^{b_1}\cdots0^{a_p}1^{b_p}\), the power-domination number is \(1\). A singleton \(\{v\}\) is power dominating exactly when either \(v\in B_i\) and every later zero-block is a singleton, or \(v\in A_1\), \(a_1\le2\), and every later zero-block is a singleton; no vertex in \(A_i\) for \(i\ge2\) works. The displayed block formula therefore counts every minimum power-dominating set.
